- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” phase.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 10–15 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values show a strong downward trend.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — often misses the “drop-off” phase.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high prices, leading to over-forecasted peaks, then under-forecasted troughs.
- Model shows poor sensitivity to the “tail” of the price distribution — especially when true values dip below 55–60, model often fails to adjust downward.
- Model exhibits lagged response — forecasts are often 1–2 days behind actual price movements, especially in the first 10 days.
- Model fails to capture the “mean reversion” pattern — tends to hold onto high forecasts even after price drops, and underestimates the speed of correction.
- Model overestimates volatility in the early part of the horizon, then underestimates it later — especially when true values show a strong downward trend.
- Model often fails to adjust for “seasonal” or “calendar” effects — e.g., price drops in late January, model doesn’t anticipate or correct for this.
